speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the number and percentage of Singaporeans above 65 years old who have registered a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and how does this compare with overall adult uptake; and (b) whether the Ministry has completed its consideration of the suggestion to further extend the waiver of the LPA Form 1 filing fee for Singaporeans beyond 31 March 2026.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is to encourage more Singaporeans to plan early for their future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In the last few years, with the launch of the Office of the Public Guardian Online portal and more visible legacy planning campaigns island-wide, we have seen a healthy uptake of LPA applications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: But many still have not made an LPA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Therefore, we want to continue to urge Singaporeans to make their LPA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Best to do so while we are still fit and healthy, and even more so as we know our population is ageing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Having an LPA in place will allow Singaporeans and our loved ones to have peace of mind, knowing there is someone we trust who will have the legal authority to make decisions on our behalf, when we no longer can.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Besides reducing the cost barrier, some members of public, especially seniors who still find it difficult to understand what an LPA is and why it is important to make an LPA, can MSF do more in terms of stepping up public education and awareness of LPA, as well as perhaps making the process easier by having it in different languages and having more support to help seniors?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In terms of running inter-agency campaigns, we are also working very closely with People's Association and various grassroots organisations on the ground, tapping on their various target audiences and their own lists, their own contacts, to make sure that we are able to get messages to as many Singaporeans as possible.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We will continue to double down on those efforts.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Of course, I will make this call in this House as well: wishing all our Members of Parliament to support this effort and help carry the messages down to their own constituencies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My question has to do with the LPA process as structured by the Office of the Public Guardian.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: One of the difficulties that we had faced in this last minute rush to the prior deadline, was that when we organised LPA sessions for residents, we face difficulties with the site being very dragging.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand that this may be a question that perhaps is better directed toward GovTech, but we are wondering, on the side of the Office of the Public Guardian, whether there has been any indication that the site has encountered difficulties?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And if so, whether there are plans to upgrade the capacity of the site going forward?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: It may also be because of other reasons, including the applicants' computer system.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, useful to know where exactly is the observation and we can follow up on that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If I may suggest, the details can be given to the Minister of State subsequently.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State, my wife and I have done our LPAs.
